definition: To have an idea, opinion, or plan in your mind.
usage_note: A very common word used for mental activity, opinions, and plans.

examples.sentence: I think it will rain later.
She thinks carefully before she speaks.
Do you think we should leave now?
examples.note: Used to ask for an opinion.

results.title: Think do tank schéma FL (french).jpg
results.description:
Diagram illustrating that there is no clear limit between the think tank and the "Do tank", but that we can classify them into three main types of "tanks". 
The Do tank (type of structure associative and collaborative that emerges in the years 2010) is expressly more oriented to the "doing" than thinking, to the production of actions or objects, not just ideas (usually with a goal of solidarity and sustainability).  Many think tanks (on the left of the graph) have been created in the service of political groups and / or industrial lobbies. Their products are "written" messages and content and audio / video prafois ... while the do tanks (phenomenon still emerging) want to be more operational (while also being able to avail themselves of political ideas), possibly in the movement of the DOI (do it yourself). In companies and administrations, we speak more often of "task force" or "project team".
